clue.text: Very important to make everybody sing about a mad man

parts.note: the whole world means everybody

indicators.note: the word sing goes around the other piece, so 'about' signals a container

parts.note: taken as written
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland, and 'mad as a hatter'

explanation.surface: Something momentous enough to set the whole planet singing about a lunatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earth-shaking in importance is described as world-shattering, an idiom for momentous.

clue.text: Mulish objections raised and natural to follow

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first, as the clue says it must follow
in a down clue a raised word reads from bottom to top, so these letters are turned around

parts.note: 'ifs and buts' are objections
a born leader is a natural one

explanation.surface: A mule's objections are lifted, and it is only natural that more follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A mulish person is obstinate like a mule, a direct synonym for unyielding.

clue.text: Proper line for two people fighting

parts.note: what is due is what is proper or owed

explanation.surface: The correct way for two people to settle a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal combat between two parties is exactly what the word names.

clue.text: Rough supporter is standing in the avenue

indicators.note: the supporter and the standing word go inside the avenue, a container

parts.note: AVE is the abbreviation for avenue
a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing puts a word upright, read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A coarse character who props things up is found standing in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough and abrasive both describe a harsh surface or a harsh manner, synonyms.

clue.text: Enthusiast embraced right partner

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as arms hold someone in an embrace

parts.note: a fiend is an addict or enthusiast, as in a fitness fiend

explanation.surface: A keen fan hugged the right person to share life with.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or companion is a close friend, a synonym in the sense of ally.

clue.text: Keeping unattached and happy

parts.note: in someone's care means in their keeping
free means not tied to anything

explanation.surface: Someone single and contented.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without worries is a happy state, so the two words are loose synonyms.

clue.text: Still figure of Ms Barker describing rubbish

indicators.note: in crosswords describing means drawing a line around, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: Sue Barker is a British tennis player turned TV presenter
tat is cheap junk

explanation.surface: A motionless figure of a TV presenter is said to portray junk.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue Barker presented the BBC's tennis and the quiz A Question of Sport; 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted figure that does not move is a statue.

clue.text: Anti-wrinkling can steer a sister off the rails

indicators.note: going off the rails is going wildly wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tin can guide a nun astray, as if the sister's habit were wrinkle-proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that resists creasing does not wrinkle, so the definition is a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: To have more than one rum, but get tipsy

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drinking more than one rum, yet becoming merry.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber a group is to exceed it in number, to have more members than it.

clue.text: First lady in the House made clergyman lose his head

indicators.note: losing a head drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: a pastor is a minister of a church

explanation.surface: A vicar who loses his head inside the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy Astor was the first woman to take a seat in the House of Commons, in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Astor was the first female MP to sit in the British House of Commons.

clue.text: Oil able to be refined in plant

indicators.note: refining reworks raw material, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oil that can be refined in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobelia is a flowering garden plant, an example of the category.

clue.text: She loved Daddy spreading treacle

indicators.note: spreading treacle moves it around, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl who adored her father, smearing syrup on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Electra was devoted to her father Agamemnon, giving the Electra complex its name.

clue.text: Emporium demands silence at work

parts.note: sh is the sound used to call for silence
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A department store insists on quiet while staff work.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large store, so it is a grand word for a retail outlet.

clue.text: Oscar's Lady of the Lake?

parts.note: Oscar Wilde wrote a comedy about a titled lady with a fan, and her title is also the name of the largest lake in England's Lake District

explanation.surface: A question about the Arthurian enchantress, attributed to a man called Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady of the Lake suggests Arthurian legend; it is Oscar Wilde's play Lady Windermere's Fan, Windermere being a lake in Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Windermere is Wilde's heroine and Windermere is a lake, so she is literally a lady of a lake.

clue.text: One and ten are confused, of course

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so the pieces are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mixing up one and ten, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means a racecourse: AINTREE near Liverpool hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a racecourse, so the answer is literally one of the courses.

clue.text: To prepare, he corrected with eraser

indicators.note: corrected text has its letters changed, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting ready, he fixed his work with a rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a play before performing is to prepare for it.

clue.text: State day centre

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
a day can mean an era, as in 'in my day', so an age

explanation.surface: A government-run day centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun, a country, but it is the verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: The average is the mean value, the middle or centre of a set of figures.

clue.text: Horror of a kind

parts.note: a version of something is a kind or variety of it

explanation.surface: A scary film of a certain type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horror' looks like the film genre with 'of a kind' qualifying it; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong dislike or loathing is an aversion, a synonym for horror in that sense.

clue.text: What makes a man hate the curse?

indicators.note: the clue asks what can be made from the words, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what drives a person to hate a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal church curse, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: The pot man accepts hard work from Rodin

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one piece takes another inside it, as a container accepts contents

parts.note: a tinker traditionally mended pots and pans
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A kettle repairer takes on hard work from a sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thinker is Rodin's famous bronze of a seated man in thought.

clue.text: In Gospel destined to be first

indicators.note: the answer sits inside these clue words, read straight across them

explanation.surface: A biblical text fated to come first.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest child is the first-born, so eldest means first in order of birth.

clue.text: Sidney is held up by crackpot who's naked

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, so this is a container

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Sid is short for Sidney

explanation.surface: Sidney is mugged by an oddball who has no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist is someone who goes without clothes, so a person who is naked.

clue.text: Mother's side seen in skirt

parts.note: ma is a word for mother; the 's is just a join
a cricket or football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Mum's figure on view in a skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is an ankle-length skirt, so it is a type of skirt.

clue.text: Flushed character calls for player to be dismissed

parts.note: flushed means red in the face
a card is a joker or eccentric character

explanation.surface: An embarrassed eccentric demands that a footballer be sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a referee shows a red card to send a player off.
explanation.definitionFit: A red card is what a referee shows to send a player off the field.

clue.text: Topper finds his talk is rambling

indicators.note: rambling talk wanders, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man finds that his speech is wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat, made of silk, is called a topper.

clue.text: They say faulty actor topped and tailed the worst parts

indicators.note: topping and tailing removes the first and last letters

parts.note: faulty sounds like Fawlty, and the actor who played Basil Fawlty in Fawlty Towers is John Cleese

explanation.surface: People claim a poor actor topped and tailed the worst roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' tells you faulty is heard as Fawlty, the hotelier of the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, played by John Cleese.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the dregs left at the bottom of wine, the worst parts.

clue.text: Organs with sounds I extracted

indicators.note: the named letter is pulled out of the word, a deletion

parts.note: noises are sounds

explanation.surface: Instruments with their sounds removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is a sense organ, so the plural names several organs.

clue.text: Official voice of the cyclist?

definitions.meaning: someone who speaks on behalf of an organisation
jokingly, a man on spoked wheels

explanation.surface: The press officer for the cycling team.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesman speaks officially for a group; humorously, a cyclist is a man of spokes.
